summary: Richard Gombrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, also studying under Walpola Rahula and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1965–2004) and Balliol College (c. 1976–2004).

Richard Hugh Robinson was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under Arthur Waley and David Friedman. He held posts at Toronto (1954) and Wisconsin-Madison (from 1961).

Richard Hughes Seager works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD c. 1982–1987). From c. 1994 to 2014, he was Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988, having studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, having studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (c. 1993–2018) and held posts at GTU (2016) and Chicago (2021).

Richard Kieckhefer is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Saint Louis University (c. 1964–1968) and the University of Texas at Austin (c. 1968–1972), joining Northwestern University in 1975.

Richard King specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster (PhD c. 1989–1992) under Daniel Mariau, he held posts at Stirling (c. 1996–2001), Vanderbilt (attested 2005–2009), and Glasgow (c. 2007–2012).
Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at North Carolina State University (c. 1995–2000) and Duke University (c. 2000).

Richard Mahoney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, earning his Master of Arts by 2002, and held a post there attested in 2001.

Richard Morris was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who studied at Battersea Training College (c. 1852–1854). He served as lecturer in English at King's College School (c. 1869–1874) and headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875).

Richard P. Boyle studied at the University of Washington and with traditional teacher Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held an attested post at the University of New Mexico in 2015.

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, and later taught at Toronto, McGill (attested 1997–2009), Leiden, and New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).
Richard Peter Hottelet is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison attested in 1971.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Breslau, Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg (c. 1885–1900), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).
Richard Polenberg was a historian who studied at Columbia University from c. 1959 to 1964 and held a faculty post at Cornell University from c. 1966 to 2011.

Richard Rorty was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (c. 1946–1952) and Yale University (c. 1952–1956). He held posts at Wellesley College (c. 1958–1961), Princeton University (attested 1987), and Stanford University (c. 1998–2005).

Richard Salomon is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He has served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998–2017) and was a visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.
Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Mehliß and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from c. 1885 to 1889.

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied at Iowa and Pennsylvania. He held posts at Texas at Austin (c. 1982–2006; dean 1999–2006), Kansas (c. 2006–2009), Oregon (c. 2009–2011), and the Field Museum of Natural History (c. 2012–2020).

Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium (c. 1887–1891). He later held academic posts at Peking University (c. 1922–1924) and Goethe University Frankfurt (c. 1924–1930).
